To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structures of the [3h]pargylinelabeled flavin‐containng polypeptide of MAO from hybrid NCB 20 cells, and its parental cells, A /J mouse brain cells and chinese hamster brain cells were analyzed and compared using SDS‐PAGE, and limited proteolysus and one‐dimensiona peptide mapping in SDS gel.

the structures of the flavin‐associated polypeptides of A and B types of MAO in hybrid NCB20 neuroblastoma cells, which are derived from A/J brain cells and Chinese brain cells, were identical to those of the corresponding MAO in the parental cells.
type A MAO and type B MAOI in hybrid cells were assigned to those of the parental cells by peptide mapping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assignment of A and B types of monoamine oxidases (MAOs) in NCB20 hybrid cells to those of the parental cells, A‐J mouse brain cells and chinese hamster brain cells.
the molecular structure of type A and type b MAO, and with the relationship between the two types of enzyme molecules.
the molecular basis of the genetic control of the two MAO types in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type A MAO is associated with the polypeptide of Mr 62,000, and that the type B MAO is associated, depending on the species, with the polypeptides of Mr 61,000 and/or 58,000.

the type A and type A‐like MAOs in the three types (NCB20 cells, Chinese hamster and A/J mouse brain) of cells are identical, that the type B MAOs are identical in Chinese hamster and NCB20, but different in A/J mouse and NCB20.
the two forms of MAO are coded by two different genes and that the two genes are located on different chromosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MAO in N20 cells is a chimera of MAOs of A/J mouse brain and Chinese hamster liver.
type A and B MAOs are distinct enzymes and that type A MAO has a single origin, while type B MAO has multiple origins.
the A/J mouse and the Chinese hamster have two types of MAOs, A and B, and that NCB20 cells express the same type of MAOs as the parental cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can identify the type of MAO in a sample by using a simple, rapid method.
we were able to identify a new class of compounds that are effective against the parasite that causes African sleeping sickness.
type B activity is associated with an enzyme with a molecular weight of 61,500, while type A activity is associated with a molecule with a molecular weight 62,000.
